title_en: Stephen Chow v. Zhongjian Rongzhen Wuxi Building Materials Technology Co., Ltd. — dispute over right to portrait and right to name
ruling_gist_en: 1. In a dispute over infringement of personality rights involving foreign elements, if both parties invoke the same law and raise no objection to the application of law, the people's court may find that the parties have made a unanimous choice regarding the governing law for the civil relationship.
keywords_en: civil; dispute over right to portrait; dispute over right to name; first instance; intermediate people's court; Shanghai; Jiangsu Province; natural person; legal person; Tort Liability Law; General Principles of the Civil Law; choice of governing law for infringement of personality rights involving foreign elements; scope of compensation for commercial use of right to name and right to portrait; discretionary factors for determining the amount of compensation; use of portrait in official website advertisements; use of portrait in magazine advertisements; infringement of commercial endorsement; tort liability; right to portrait
full_text_en:
Zhou Xingchi v. Zhongjian Rongzhen Wuxi Building Materials Technology Co., Ltd. — Dispute over Portrait Rights and Name Rights

【Ruling Summary】

1. In a foreign-related tort dispute over personality rights, where both parties invoke the same law and raise no objection to the application of that law, the people's court may find that the parties have made a unanimous choice of the governing law for the relevant civil relationship.

2. Where the right to name and the right to portrait have commercialized use functions, and a party makes a claim solely on the basis of the Tort Liability Law, the spiritual interests and property value of such personality rights may be protected jointly, and attorney's fees falling within reasonable expenses shall be included in the scope of damages for personality rights.

3. In determining the amount of damages at its discretion, the people's court shall conduct a comprehensive evaluation based on factors including the type of right, the method of infringement, the degree of infringement, the status and economic conditions of the infringed party and the infringer, the gains obtained, the type of fault, and other relevant circumstances.

Plaintiff: Zhou Xingchi (CHIAU, SING CHI), male, 55 years old, Han Chinese, resident of Wan Chai, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

Defendant: Zhongjian Rongzhen Wuxi Building Materials Technology Co., Ltd., domiciled at Fengming Road, Huangtang Industrial Park, Xuxiake Town, Jiangyin City, Jiangsu Province.

Legal Representative: Zhang Dexiang, General Manager of the Company.

Plaintiff Zhou Xingchi filed an action with the Shanghai No. 1 Intermediate People's Court against Defendant Zhongjian Rongzhen Wuxi Building Materials Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Zhongjian Rongzhen Building Materials Company") for a dispute over portrait rights and name rights.

Plaintiff's Allegations: In January 2017, Plaintiff Zhou Xingchi, based on feedback from fans, discovered that Defendant Zhongjian Rongzhen Building Materials Company had published a promotional advertisement on the most prominent position of its official website, reading "City Forest joins hands with 'Xing Ye' to witness the true kung fu of ecological wall panels." This advertisement scrolled together with two other promotional advertisements targeting consumers and agents respectively, which read "Whole-house quick installation, saving worry, labor, time, and effort, 7 days from rough to luxury" and "Brand investment solicitation in Greater China, only one agent per city, nationwide hot opening now." Meanwhile, Plaintiff also found that Defendant had published a promotional advertisement on the "Entrepreneurial State" website reading "City Forest integrated wall decoration joins hands with the King of Comedy Zhou Xingchi to witness the true kung fu of ecological wall panels," with a caption beside Plaintiff's photograph reading "Chinese-language comedy actor, director, screenwriter, supervisor, producer, presenter. Representative work: *Kung Fu Hustle*." On January 13, 2017, Plaintiff sent a lawyer's letter to Defendant, demanding cessation of infringement, restoration of reputation, elimination of adverse effects, and an apology. In September 2017, a friend of Plaintiff discovered the *Lvban* magazine (Issue No. 2 of 2017, General Issue No. 243) at Hongqiao Railway Station. The advertisement page of that issue published a promotional advertisement reading "City Forest, whole-house quick installation, bring the forest home," with the most prominent display showing "Zhou Xingchi, star of *Kung Fu Hustle*, joins hands with City Forest environmental protection industry" and "Representative works: *Kung Fu Hustle*, *The Yangtze River No. 7*, *A Chinese Odyssey*, *Shaolin Soccer*, *The Mermaid*, etc. Zhou Xingchi is one of the iconic figures in Chinese-language cinema. From his nonsensical comedic performance style, audiences can often perceive some profound truths revealed behind the comedy. *The Mermaid*, released earlier this year, brought environmental topics to the public's attention, which coincidentally aligns with City Forest's original intention of 'ecological environmental protection.'" The promotional advertisements published by Defendant on its official website, the Entrepreneurial State website, and in *Lvban* magazine all used Plaintiff's portrait to solicit business, infringing upon Plaintiff's portrait rights. In summary, Defendant, for profit-making purposes, used Plaintiff's name and portrait in advertisements without Plaintiff's consent, violating Plaintiff's name rights and portrait rights. Plaintiff requested the court to order: 1. Defendant to immediately cease using Plaintiff's portrait, name, and stage name on its official website (www.360cssl.com) and in *Lvban* magazine; 2. Defendant to pay damages of 31,125,001 yuan, including 30 million yuan for property damages, 1.125 million yuan for reasonable expenses, and 1 yuan for moral damages; 3. Defendant to publish apologies on its official website (www.360cssl.com), in *Lvban* magazine, on Sina, Sohu, and in a national newspaper for infringement of Plaintiff's name rights and portrait rights, for a duration of 90 days.

Defendant's Defense: Defendant acknowledged the facts alleged by Plaintiff Zhou Xingchi and stated that the company had indeed used Plaintiff's portrait in advertisements without his consent, but did not confirm that it had infringed upon Zhou Xingchi's name rights, leaving the matter to the court's lawful examination. Defendant had ceased using Plaintiff's portrait on its official website (www.360cssl.com) and agreed to publish an apology on the official website for the infringement of Plaintiff's portrait rights, leaving the duration to the court's lawful examination. Defendant argued that the amount of damages claimed by Plaintiff was excessively high; generally, courts determine damages within a range of 500,000 yuan, and requested the court to examine the damages claimed by Plaintiff in accordance with the law.

Facts Found by the Shanghai No. 1 Intermediate People's Court:

On January 11, 2017, the home page of Defendant Zhongjian Rongzhen Building Materials Company's official website (www.360cssl.com) displayed a promotional advertisement reading "Bring the forest home, 7 days from rough to luxury, saving worry, labor, time, and effort." Beside this advertisement was a photograph of Plaintiff Zhou Xingchi, with text below reading "City Forest joins hands with 'Xing Ye' to witness the true kung fu of ecological wall panels." Additionally, on the webpage (www.360cssl.com/index.php/Show/index/cid/196/id/215.html), under the "Terminal Style VI Display" section, there was a promotional advertisement reading "City Forest joins hands with 'Xing Ye' to witness the true kung fu of ecological wall panels." This advertisement featured Plaintiff's photograph and was displayed together with the promotional slogan "Whole-house quick installation, saving worry, labor, time, and money, 7 days from rough to luxury" on the same page.

On June 19, 2017, on the website page of Defendant Zhongjian Rongzhen Building Materials Company (www.360cssl.com/index.php/Show/index/cid/196/id/215.html), under the "Terminal Style VI Display" section, the same promotional advertisement reading "City Forest joins hands with 'Xing Ye' to witness the true kung fu of ecological wall panels" appeared, accompanied by Plaintiff Zhou Xingchi's photograph and displayed together with the promotional slogan "Whole-house quick installation, saving worry, labor, time, and money, 7 days from rough to luxury."

On June 19, 2017, the "Entrepreneurial State" website (bd.chuangzhanw.com/cssl/) and its subpage (bd.chuangzhanw.com/cssl/?=BDPCHX00590) both displayed a promotional advertisement reading "City Forest integrated wall decoration joins hands with the King of Comedy Zhou Xingchi to witness the true kung fu of ecological wall panels," with a caption beside an illustration of Plaintiff Zhou Xingchi's photograph reading "Chinese-language comedy actor, director, screenwriter, supervisor, producer, presenter. Representative work: *Kung Fu Hustle*."

On September 5, 2017, Yu Meina, the authorized agent of Plaintiff Zhou Xingchi, purchased a copy of *Lvban* magazine (Issue No. 2 of 2017, General Issue No. 243) at the "Yuetu Business VIP Lounge" at the departure level, South Gate 6 of Shanghai Hongqiao Railway Station. Defendant Zhongjian Rongzhen Building Materials Company had published an advertisement in *Lvban* magazine. The advertisement page of that issue featured an article titled "Whole-house quick installation, 7 days from rough to luxury," above which appeared the promotional advertisements "City Forest, whole-house quick installation, bring the forest home" and "From Bologna, Europe, creating urban ecological living space." To the right of these advertisements was a photograph of Plaintiff Zhou Xingchi bearing his portrait and signature, with small text reading "Zhou Xingchi, star of the *Kung Fu Hustle* cast, joins hands with City Forest environmental protection industry," and accompanying text: "Representative works: *Kung Fu Hustle*, *The Yangtze River No. 7*, *A Chinese Odyssey*, *Shaolin Soccer*, *The Mermaid*, etc. Zhou Xingchi is one of the iconic figures in Chinese-language cinema. From his nonsensical comedic performance style, audiences can often perceive some profound truths revealed behind the comedy. *The Mermaid*, released earlier this year, brought environmental topics to the public's attention, which coincidentally aligns with City Forest's original intention of 'ecological environmental protection.'"

It was additionally found that *Lvban* magazine has a domestic unified serial number CN11-4858/G0, is a nationally distributed publication, with the competent authority being China Railway Corporation, and the sponsoring and publishing entity being China Railway Publishing House Co., Ltd. The magazine is a bi-monthly, priced at 15 yuan, and its railway station and train distribution network includes Beijing, Shanghai, Tianjin, Hangzhou, Wuhan, Nanjing, Jinan, Fuzhou, Shenyang, Dalian, among others.

It was further found that on January 13, 2017, Plaintiff Zhou Xingchi, through his attorney, sent a lawyer's letter to Defendant Zhongjian Rongzhen Building Materials Company, stating: "Your company has published a promotional advertisement on its official website (www.360cssl.com) reading 'City Forest joins hands with "Xing Ye" to witness the true kung fu of ecological wall panels,' and used my client's photograph on the homepage and in VI displays to solicit business. Pursuant to Article 120 of the *General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC*: 'If a citizen's right to name, right to portrait, right to reputation, or right to honor is infringed, he or she has the right to demand cessation of infringement, restoration of reputation, elimination of adverse effects, and an apology, and may also demand compensation for losses.' Your company's unauthorized use of my client's stage name and photograph for commercial publicity constitutes infringement and shall bear tort liability. In light of the above facts, my client hereby authorizes this attorney to formally notify your company as follows: 1. Within three days of the issuance of this letter, your company shall publicly clarify that my client has never authorized your company to use his name, stage name, or photograph, and has never engaged in any form of commercial cooperation with your company. 2. Within three days of the issuance of this letter, your company shall immediately delete from its official website the promotional advertisement reading 'City Forest joins hands with "Xing Ye" to witness the true kung fu of ecological wall panels,' and immediately cease using my client's stage name and/or photograph for commercial publicity. Your company's actions have seriously infringed upon my client's legitimate rights and interests, including his name rights and portrait rights. This attorney has completed evidence collection on behalf of my client. My client will file a lawsuit with the court to pursue all economic, reputational, and other losses caused by your company. This letter is hereby given." The letter was sent via EMS and received by the security guard on January 15, 2017.

It was also found that on September 25, 2017, Plaintiff Zhou Xingchu, as Party A, entered into a *Retainer Agreement for the Engagement of a Lawyer* with Beijing Century (Shanghai) Law Firm, engaging a lawyer from that firm to represent him in the case against Defendant Zhongjian Rongzhen Building Materials Company for infringement of name rights and portrait rights. The agreed attorney's fee totaled 1,125,000 yuan, representing the full fee for the firm's representation in the first instance, second instance, and enforcement proceedings. Plaintiff remitted the above amount to Beijing Century (Shanghai) Law Firm via bank transfer.

During the trial, Defendant Zhongjian Rongzhen Building Materials Company admitted that the advertising images on its official website and in *Lvban* magazine were purchased by it from Zhongshan Yibo Company and then provided to a third party for publication, and confirmed that the portrait and signature in the advertisements were those of Plaintiff Zhou Xingchi. Both parties agreed that "Xing Ye" referred to Plaintiff Zhou Xingchi. As of the time Plaintiff filed the lawsuit, Defendant had already ceased publishing the advertisements on its official website, the Entrepreneurial State website, and in *Lvban* magazine.

Opinion of the Shanghai No. 1 Intermediate People's Court:

This case is a dispute over infringement of portrait rights and name rights. As Plaintiff Zhou Xingchi is a resident of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, the application of law in this case shall be determined by reference to the *Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Law of the PRC on Choice of Law for Foreign-Related Civil Relations (I)*. Paragraph 2 of Article 8 of that Interpretation provides: "Where the parties all invoke the law of the same country and raise no objection to the application of that law, the people's court may find that the parties have made a choice of the law applicable to the foreign-related civil relationship." Plaintiff brought this action in accordance with Articles 99 and 100 of the *General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC*, Article 141 of the *Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC (Trial Implementation)*, and Article 2 of the *Tort Liability Law of the PRC*. Defendant Zhongjian Rongzhen Building Materials Company also defended on the basis of the same laws. Therefore, the court finds that the parties have made a choice of the governing law for the civil relationship, and this case shall be tried in accordance with the laws of Mainland China.

The issues in dispute are: 1. Whether Defendant Zhongjian Rongzhen Building Materials Company's actions infringed upon Plaintiff Zhou Xingchi's portrait rights and name rights; and 2. If infringement is established, what tort liability shall Defendant bear.

Regarding Issue 1: Whether the actions of Defendant Zhongjian Rongzhen Building Materials Company constitute infringement.

The court holds that, first, the right to portrait is the right of a natural person to enjoy interests in his or her own portrait and to exclude others from infringing upon it, and is an important part of a natural person's personality rights. Article 100 of the *General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC* provides: "Citizens shall enjoy the right to portrait. Without the consent of the person concerned, no one may use the portrait of a citizen for profit-making purposes." Article 139 of the *Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC (Trial Implementation)* provides: "Using another person's portrait for profit-making purposes without the consent of the person concerned, such as in advertisements, trademarks, or store window displays, shall be deemed an infringement of the citizen's right to portrait." Plaintiff Zhou Xingchi's right to portrait is protected by law; without Zhou Xingchi's permission, no one may use his portrait for profit-making purposes. Defendant used Plaintiff Zhou Xingchi's portrait on its official website (www.360cssl.com), the Entrepreneurial State website (bd.chuangzhanw.com/cssl/), and in *Lvban* magazine. Such actions constitute infringement of Plaintiff's right to portrait.

Second, Article 99 of the *General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC* provides: "Citizens shall enjoy the right to name, and have the right to decide, use, and change their names in accordance with legal provisions, and shall prohibit others from interfering with, misappropriating, or counterfeiting their names." Article 141 of the *Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC (Trial Implementation)* provides: "Misappropriating or counterfeiting another person's name or title, causing damage, shall be deemed an infringement of the right to name or right to title." The object of the right to name includes not only the full name, but also other symbols of identity that can establish a corresponding relationship with a specific natural person, such as pseudonyms, stage names, and nicknames. Defendant's misappropriation of Plaintiff's name and stage name in the advertisements constitutes infringement of Plaintiff's right to name.

Finally, Defendant failed to provide evidence that it had obtained a license to use Plaintiff's portrait or name rights. For profit-making purposes, Defendant used Plaintiff's portrait and name (stage name) in its promotional advertisements on websites and in magazines, with prominent display, thereby infringing upon Plaintiff's portrait rights and name rights.

Regarding Issue 2: What tort liability shall Defendant Zhongjian Rongzhen Building Materials Company bear.

The objects protected by the right to portrait and the right to name are the personality interests embodied in the portrait and name. Article 2 of the *Tort Liability Law of the PRC* provides: "Those who infringe upon civil rights and interests shall bear tort liability in accordance with this Law. The civil rights and interests referred to in this Law shall include personal and property rights and interests such as the right to life, right to health, right to name, right to reputation, right to honor, right to portrait, right to privacy, right to marital autonomy, right to guardianship, ownership, usufructuary rights, security interests, copyrights, patent rights, exclusive rights to use trademarks, rights of discovery, equity, and inheritance rights." Article 15 provides: "The methods of bearing tort liability shall mainly include: (1) cessation of infringement; (2) removal of obstruction; (3) elimination of danger; (4) return of property; (5) restoration to original condition; (6) compensation for losses; (7) apology; and (8) elimination of adverse effects and restoration of reputation. The above methods of bearing tort liability may be applied separately or in combination." Where a natural person's right to name, right to portrait, right to reputation, or right to honor is infringed, the person has the right to demand cessation of infringement, restoration of reputation, elimination of adverse effects, and apology, and may also demand compensation for losses. Where a person's personal rights and interests are infringed upon, causing serious mental damage, the infringed party may claim compensation for moral damages. In this case, Defendant, a for-profit legal person, used Plaintiff Zhou Xingchi's portrait and name without his consent, thereby infringing upon Plaintiff's portrait rights and name rights, and shall bear corresponding tort liability in accordance with the law. In this regard, the court makes the following specific findings:

First, regarding the cessation of infringement. Defendant Zhongjian Rongzhen Building Materials Company stated during the trial that after receiving Plaintiff Zhou Xingchi's lawyer's letter, it had ceased the infringing conduct. Plaintiff also acknowledged that as of the time of filing this lawsuit, no further infringement by Defendant had been discovered. As there is currently no evidence that Defendant continues to infringe upon Plaintiff Zhou Xingchi's portrait rights and name rights on its website and in magazines, Plaintiff's claim for immediate cessation of infringement lacks sufficient factual basis and is not supported by the court.

Second, regarding compensation for losses. First, a portrait is a visual image of a natural person's appearance reproduced on a material carrier through painting, photography, film, television, video, sculpture, or other forms. As an image symbol of a natural person, a portrait is closely related to that person's external image and personality. It directly concerns the person's dignity and the social evaluation of their image. On one hand, a portrait and a name can distinguish one natural person from another and reflect the personal dignity and reputation of the right holders of the right to portrait and the right to name, constituting their spiritual interests. On the other hand, a natural person's use of a portrait or name can generate certain commercial benefits. The plaintiff, Zhou Xingchi, as a well-known artist and actor, can obtain corresponding economic benefits through activities such as participating in film and television programs and advertising endorsements. His right to portrait and right to name have certain commercial exploitation value. The infringement by the defendant, Zhongjian Rongzhen Building Materials Company, upon the plaintiff's right to portrait and right to name resulted in partial damage to the economic interests contained within the personality rights of the plaintiff, impairing the commercial value of the plaintiff's image. Therefore, compensation shall be made for the property losses caused by the illegal use of the plaintiff's portrait and name. Second, Article 20 of the Tort Liability Law of the People's Republic of China provides that where a person's personal rights and interests are infringed upon, causing property losses, compensation shall be made according to the losses suffered by the infringed person; if the losses of the infringed person are difficult to determine and the infringer has gained benefits, compensation shall be made according to the benefits obtained; if the benefits obtained by the infringer are also difficult to determine, and the infringed person and the infringer cannot agree on the amount of compensation, and a lawsuit is filed with a people's court, the people's court shall determine the amount of compensation based on the actual circumstances. Paragraph 1 of Article 18 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Civil Disputes over Infringement of Personal Rights and Interests through the Use of Information Networks stipulates that reasonable expenses incurred by the infringed person to stop the infringing act may be determined as property losses under Article 20 of the Tort Liability Law. Reasonable expenses include reasonable costs for investigation and evidence collection by the infringed person or their agent ad litem. The people's court may, based on the parties' requests and the specific circumstances of the case, include attorney fees that comply with relevant state regulations within the scope of compensation. Paragraph 2 stipulates that if the property losses suffered by the infringed person due to infringement of personal rights and interests, or the benefits obtained by the infringer, cannot be determined, the people's court may determine the amount of compensation within the range of RMB 500,000 or less based on the specific circumstances of the case. The court is of the opinion that the above judicial interpretation is a special provision applicable to cases where the infringing act is committed on an information network. For damages arising from other types of infringing acts that also exist in the case, the general provisions of the Tort Liability Law shall still apply. Finally, in this case, the plaintiff requested that the compensation amount be calculated by reference to the endorsement fee for Coca-Cola. However, the evidence he provided was not directly related to this case and was insufficient to prove the losses suffered. He also failed to provide evidence to prove the defendant's gains. Since the plaintiff's property losses or the defendant's gains from the infringement are difficult to determine, and the parties were unable to reach an agreement on the compensation amount, the court, based on the actual circumstances of the case, determined the compensation amount to be RMB 580,000 as it deemed appropriate. This includes: 1. Property damages of RMB 500,000. The plaintiff, as a well-known actor and director, enjoys wide public recognition. The defendant, as a for-profit legal person, for its own marketing needs, used the plaintiff's portrait and name without authorization on its company website and the Zhaoshangbang website in January and June 2017, and published an advertisement in *Companion* magazine (Issue 2, 2017) thereby committing the infringing act. The above acts not only infringed upon the plaintiff's personal dignity but also harmed the interests arising from the right holder's own use or authorization to others to use the portrait and name. Ultimately, this would damage the fair competition order of honest business operations and the legitimate rights and interests of other operators and consumers. The court noted that after the plaintiff sent a lawyer's letter, the defendant had not ceased the infringement as of June 19, 2017. In September of the same year, *Companion* magazine appeared at Hongqiao Railway Station. The magazine's distribution scope on railway stations and trains covered most of the high-speed rail multiple unit (EMU) operating sections nationwide. Thus, the infringement involved in this case had a wide scope of influence and a relatively long duration. Although the defendant argued that it had spent RMB 90,000 to purchase the plaintiff's photos from a third party, it knowingly used the plaintiff's portrait and name to create and publish the advertisements in question without obtaining the plaintiff's consent, thus showing subjective fault. Therefore, considering factors such as the plaintiff's professional status, fame, and circumstances of portrait licensing; the duration of the defendant's infringing act, the degree of subjective fault, the scope of the infringing advertisements, the public nature of the website, the circulation of the magazine, and the potential impact, the court determined property damages of RMB 500,000. 2. Reasonable expenses of RMB 80,000. Attorney fees are the result of the autonomy of will between the client and the lawyer, and the court does not interfere. The judicial interpretation clearly stipulates that reasonable expenses incurred by the infringed person to stop the infringing act constitute property losses of the infringed person. The plaintiff claimed reasonable expenses of RMB 1.125 million. However, in fact, this amount included matters relating to the first instance, second instance, and enforcement. The court is of the opinion that the expenses the plaintiff requires the defendant to bear in this case should be limited to a reasonable range. Therefore, comprehensively considering factors such as the litigation costs for the plaintiff to stop the infringement, the subject matter of the case, the amount of compensation awarded, the complexity of the case, the work volume of the lawyers, and the relevant attorney fee standards, the court determined reasonable expenses of RMB 80,000.

Third, regarding compensation for mental distress. Article 22 of the Tort Liability Law of the People's Republic of China provides that where a person's personal rights and interests are infringed upon, causing serious mental distress to the infringed person, the infringed person may claim compensation for mental distress. Paragraph 1 of Article 8 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Determination of Liability for Compensation for Mental Distress in Civil Torts provides that where a tort causes mental distress but does not result in serious consequences, the victim's claim for compensation for mental distress is generally not supported; however, the people's court may, depending on the circumstances, order the infringer to cease the infringement, restore the victim's reputation, eliminate the impact, and make an apology. As mentioned above, in this case, the defendant's infringement upon the plaintiff's right to portrait and right to name caused partial damage to the economic interests contained within the personality rights, but it did not reach the level of serious mental distress. Therefore, the court does not support the plaintiff's claim for compensation for mental distress in the amount of RMB 1.

Fourth, regarding an apology. The purpose of an apology is to make the relevant audience aware of the truth and eliminate the adverse impact on the infringed person. The method of apology should be determined by reference to the specific manner and scope of influence of the infringing act. Regarding the plaintiff's claim that the defendant should publicly apologize to the plaintiff on its official website (www.360cssl.com), in *Companion* magazine, on Sina, Sohu, and in a national newspaper, the court is of the opinion that the scope of the public apology should be commensurate with the degree of influence caused by the infringing act. Considering the specific circumstances of the infringement, such as the form, scope, and content of the defendant's use of the plaintiff's photos, the court supports the plaintiff's claim that the defendant should publish an apology statement on its official website (www.360cssl.com) and in *Companion* magazine.

In summary, part of the plaintiff's claims are legally grounded and shall be supported accordingly. Pursuant to Article 110 and Article 179 of the General Provisions of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 2, Article 6, Article 15, and Article 20 of the Tort Liability Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 99, Article 100, and Paragraph 1 of Article 120 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 139 and Article 141 of the Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China (for Trial Implementation), Article 18 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Civil Disputes over Infringement of Personal Rights and Interests through the Use of Information Networks, Paragraph 1 of Article 8 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Determination of Liability for Compensation for Mental Distress in Civil Torts, and Article 28, Paragraph 1 of Article 64, and Article 149 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Shanghai No. 1 Intermediate People's Court rendered the following judgment on April 8, 2019:

I. The defendant, Zhongjian Rongzhen Wuxi Building Materials Technology Co., Ltd., shall compensate the plaintiff, Zhou Xingchi, in the amount of RMB 580,000 (including reasonable expenses of RMB 80,000) within ten days from the effective date of this judgment;

II. The defendant, Zhongjian Rongzhen Wuxi Building Materials Technology Co., Ltd., shall, within ten days from the effective date of this judgment, publish an apology statement on its official website (www.360cssl.com) and in *Companion* magazine, respectively, for a duration of 30 days (the layout and content of the publication are subject to court approval). If the defendant fails to comply or the compliance does not meet the requirements of this judgment within the specified period, the court will publish the main contents of this judgment in a nationally distributed publication, and the relevant costs shall be borne by the defendant, Zhongjian Rongzhen Wuxi Building Materials Technology Co., Ltd.;

III. The other claims of the plaintiff, Zhou Xingchi, are dismissed.

After the first-instance judgment was rendered, neither party appealed, and the first-instance judgment has taken legal effect.
